title: Give a generated image a next step
problem: An image result needed somewhere to live and a way to change one part of it.
change: Projects, scenes, panels, a gallery and mask-based revision formed the first working loop.
next: Organisation became part of making the image, setting up the later gallery redesign.

title: Make the web build repeatable
problem: The application existed before its deployment tag stream.
change: Versioned web deployment checkpoints began, with follow-up patches to build and image metadata.
next: Repeatable builds made frequent, small corrections practical. This is a deployment marker, not the origin date.

title: Put browsing and organisation together
problem: Separate gallery and browse screens split the same task across two places.
change: A unified gallery added a hierarchy tree and bulk assignment.
next: The same organised image could then become a reference in a conversation.

title: Carry the reference into the conversation
problem: An image and the conversation about it needed a direct handoff.
change: Gallery-to-chat integration connected the visual workspace to iterative chat.
next: Conversations became another way to work with assets, alongside generation and revision.

title: Give reusable agent setup a home
problem: Useful coding instructions and tools were accumulating around individual sessions.
change: Metaclaude began as a versioned configuration repository.
next: Skills and selective linking developed around the distinction between shared setup and machine state.

title: Let different media share the workspace
problem: Creative work also produced audio and documents that needed context.
change: The gallery broadened into a multi-type asset surface.
next: The organising model could serve a longer workflow than image generation alone.

title: Draw a stable engine boundary
problem: A chat client needed to follow a tool-using agent through a long turn.
change: Claude Engine established a stable HTTP and streamed-event boundary.
next: Other clients and runtimes could integrate around an explicit conversation contract.

title: Discover tools without waking every server
problem: Tool discovery depended on separately running capabilities.
change: A schema cache gave clients a reusable catalogue.
next: The bridge could grow while keeping discovery separate from individual server availability.

title: Make remembered relationships usable
problem: Useful decisions and connections were scattered through conversations.
change: Knowledge graph tools exposed triples, events, decisions, beliefs and questions.
next: Reading the graph still required links back to the source; extraction and grounding became the next concern.

title: Choose the web as the product surface
problem: The desktop wrapper added another maintained boundary to a web application.
change: PanelForge chose a web-only direction and removed the NativePHP/Electron layer.
next: Development could focus on the browser workspace and its mobile behaviour.

title: Give separate tools a common bridge
problem: Independent stdio tools needed a consistent service boundary.
change: All eleven bridge servers moved onto mcp-mux.
next: New resources could join the shared gateway without each client learning a new transport.

title: Add a second runtime with its own adapter
problem: Codex had a different upstream protocol from Claude.
change: The first tagged Codex Engine adapter used app-server JSON-RPC behind the common client envelope.
next: The next engine could join an established client pattern while keeping its own runtime integration.

title: Bring three runtimes into one interface
problem: Switching engines should preserve a recognisable conversation surface.
change: OpenCode joined Claude and Codex through the shared streaming path and reusable profiles.
next: Parity made differences in recovery, permissions and runtime behaviour easier to address explicitly.

title: Treat opening chat on a phone as a feature
problem: A long mobile loading hang made the workspace hard to enter.
change: The release reduced conversation payloads and revised timeout and reload handling.
next: The practical success of a feature also depended on getting into it reliably.

title: Handle the interruption inside voice chat
problem: A spoken conversation could be interrupted while the agent was still working.
change: The Apple client added interruption recovery, standby, local commands and spoken questions.
next: Voice interaction needed deliberate turn state, not just speech playback.

title: Share setup while keeping state local
problem: Another coding runtime needed the portable workbench pattern.
change: Metacodex selectively linked portable files and generated configuration from local overlays.
next: Shared skills could travel while authentication, caches and sessions stayed machine-local.

title: Look up the evidence before keeping a fact
problem: Analysis could invent duplicate names or produce incomplete graph records.
change: A grounded agentic analysis loop required evidence lookup, validation and a terminal receipt.
next: Candidate resolution and later curation could build on an explicit evidence boundary.

title: Give projects a workspace above them
problem: A growing project collection needed another level of organisation.
change: Workspaces became the protected top level, with migration and move support.
next: The same gallery hierarchy could now separate broader bodies of work.

title: Make the same composition move
problem: A graphic preview and its video export needed to agree.
change: Animated shader backgrounds joined Kitforge, using the same rendering function for preview and export.
next: A browser composition could become a still image or a looping clip.

title: Connect a native canvas to the tool gateway
problem: Useful work also lived outside a browser, on a drawing canvas.
change: Freeform joined the gateway after stateful InfinitySketch proxy work.
next: Native surfaces could participate through explicit resources and transport handling.

title: Review delegated work across runtimes
problem: Delegation needed a durable handoff and a place for lessons from completed work.
change: Helm added Claude and Codex captains with a shared learning protocol.
next: A workbench could improve its working practices as well as its tools.

title: Check policy where an agent starts
problem: Written model instructions needed an execution check.
change: A model-policy hook validated agent starts and shared retry guidance.
next: The portable workbench gained a testable boundary around how delegated work begins.

title: Keep the answer after a broken stream
problem: A client connection could disappear while a tool-using turn continued.
change: An outbox and ordered recovery timeline retained the completed result for later collection.
next: Recovery could restore the work in order; server restart recovery remained a separate problem.

title: Check a quiet agent before interrupting it
problem: A long silence could be healthy waiting rather than a dead runtime.
change: Bounded liveness probes replaced interruption based only on silence.
next: Recovery decisions could depend on the actual upstream state.

title: Give a follow-up a route into ongoing work
problem: A new instruction needed an explicit meaning while a turn was already running.
change: Queue and injection steering gave follow-ups deliberate handling.
next: Users could refine ongoing work with a defined control contract.

title: Enforce the selected native tools
problem: A visible permission choice needed to constrain the runtime itself.
change: Native tool profiles were validated against the installed catalogue and enforced on resumed and forked sessions.
next: The client choice became an engine boundary with tests across session lifecycles.

title: Make the development history browsable
problem: Imported coding transcripts were difficult to navigate as a growing collection.
change: Code History added full-page list, day and week views.
next: Showing more sessions exposed a new problem: making a crowded week understandable.

title: Turn the crowded week into a digest
problem: A dense week view made the important sessions hard to pick out.
change: Daily activity bars, selected digest cards and expandable session strips gave the week a readable hierarchy.
next: The next interaction became deciding whether a session was worth opening.

title: Read the story before opening the session
problem: A title alone did not explain the work inside a coding session.
change: A larger session peek showed the beginning, ending and available analysis, with previous and next navigation.
next: Skimming became a meaningful step between the weekly overview and a full transcript.

title: Give the transcript room to be read
problem: Opening a read-only coding session still constrained the actual reading surface.
change: The transcript gained the whole pane, following digest, preview and typed-message corrections.
next: A sequence of patch checkpoints improved the complete journey from overview to reading.
